text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- National Electric Power Authority may soon introduce special cards for the measurement and billing of electricity consumption to consumers. An official said experiments on the cards have already begun.
- 12,000 telephone lines destroyed by fire in Benin City, leaving communications in the southern city in a state of near paralysis.

- Non-scheduled cargo and passenger flights run the risk of being turned back or grounded, as aviation authorities introduce measures to halt the violation of Nigerian airspace and the evasion of payment for the right to cross it.
- National Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers calls for dialogue to avert possible crisis following the sacking of 33 of its members from an oil service company in southeastern Port Harcourt.
- Official inauguration of the $4 billion Liquefied Natural Gas project is likely to take place on February 27.
- Insiders have expressed fears that new appointments of top management at UBA, one of Nigeria's big three banks, may not have the approval of the central bank.
- Strong indications have emerged that government may cut port charges to boost activity and increase competitiveness.
- Travellers shun domestic air services as harmattan wind blows dust from the Sahara desert creating very poor visibility.
- Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation may have started exploring possibility of raising funds from the capital market to pay depositors' claims from distressed banks.
- Public sector workers are asking for wage increases of 700 percent.
